checks: Cold read, threshold zero: the finite cover gives the union bound. A finite Borel measure on Euclidean space is concentrated on its support, so the cap masses may be taken either in the ambient space or inside K. Zero total mass also gives the asserted inequality.

Cold read, positive threshold: for a nonzero normal, the halfspace indicators converge pointwise off the limiting boundary, which is null. The tail tends to zero by finiteness of the measure, even if support is unbounded. For A_i > alpha > 0 the target A_i - alpha lies strictly between zero and the original mass, so continuity gives a finite threshold at or beyond the original one. Strict monotonicity is unnecessary.

Cold read, surviving region: each removed open tail has mass A_i - alpha by nullity of the cutting boundary. The union bound therefore gives the stated lower bound on the common closed convex remainder. A nonpositive lower bound already proves (1). Otherwise the remainder has positive mass and qualifies for the hereditary premise. Every original halfspace meets it in at most alpha mass, including uncut caps and the cut caps whose entire retained bands in K have exactly alpha mass. The hereditary point lies in at least one original closed covering halfspace, including the case of a boundary point, so g times the remaining mass is at most alpha. Division uses g > 0.

For ordinary volume the support is the convex body itself and hyperplanes are null. Each positive-volume closed convex restriction is compact and full-dimensional. The full-mass case of 6769574fc1bd9f8d applies and supplies the required point of the restriction. Grünbaum's primary source also states the centroid conclusion in its proof of Theorem 2, §3, pp. 1259–1260.

At alpha = min_i A_i all positive parts are exactly A_i - alpha, including zero differences. At alpha = A_(3), all terms beyond the first two vanish and the first two are A_(1) - A_(3) and A_(2) - A_(3), including ties. Zero padding when m < 3 adds zero terms. For D >= 2 the binomial terms of degrees zero, one, and two give (1 + 1/D)^D > 2, while log(1 + 1/D) < 1/D gives the upper bound e < 3. For D = 1, 1/gamma_1 = 2 and alpha = A_(2) yields the two-largest bound, including a zero-padded second entry.

Simplex equality: the barycentric coordinates sum to one, so the threshold 1/(D+1) covers. Under homothety about v_i of ratio D/(D+1), lambda_i is transformed into 1/(D+1) + D lambda_i/(D+1). The image is exactly the designated cap, and all cap volumes are gamma_D V by the volume determinant. With alpha and a both equal to gamma_D V, (1), (2) for m = D+1, and (3) are equalities. For D = 1 the two half-intervals give equality as well. This is an equality example.

summary: The parallel cuts prove the hereditary-depth bound for every nonnegative threshold, including unbounded support. The centroid specialization, overlap estimate, ordered cap bounds, and simplex equality are valid.
